classes.name: Halalan sa Pangulo
classes.finest_note: Precinct (clustered precinct) election returns on the transparency sites since 2016; before automation (2010) only the national canvass by province and city is official.
classes.note: Direct election by plurality, single round, six-year term with no re-election since 1987 (Art. VII, Sec. 4). Under the 1935 Constitution a four-year term with one re-election (1935 six years, no re-election); the 1973 Constitution as amended in 1981 brought the 1981 direct election, and the 1986 snap election was called by Batas Pambansa Blg. 883. The 1943 choice by the KALIBAPI National Assembly is the separate class president_1943. Overseas voting since 2004.
classes.locator: https://www.comelec.gov.ph/?r=References/RelatedLaws/Constitution/1987Constitution/Article7 (Section 4: elected by direct vote of the people for a term of six years)

classes.note: 24 senators elected nationwide at large, half every three years since 1992 (all 24 in 1987 and 1992), by plurality block vote with up to twelve votes per ballot; six-year terms, two consecutive at most (Art. classes.name: Halalan sa Kapulungan ng mga Kinatawan (distritong pambatas)
classes.finest_note: District canvasses and precinct returns on the transparency sites since 2016; before automation only the proclaimed winners are on record with COMELEC.
classes.note: Single-member legislative districts apportioned among provinces, cities, and Metro Manila, first past the post, three-year terms, three consecutive at most (Art. VI, Sec. 5 and 7). Continues the Philippine Assembly (1907-1916) and the House of Representatives of 1916-1935 and 1946-1972; the unicameral National Assembly (1935-1941), the 1943 KALIBAPI assembly, and the Batasang Pambansa (1978-1986) are separate classes. Vacancies are filled by special elections (listed by COMELEC); the 1941 election chose the House of the restored bicameral Congress, which first met in 1945.

classes.name: Pambansang Asamblea (1935-1941)
classes.note: Unicameral National Assembly of the Commonwealth, 98 members from single-member districts, elected in 1935 and 1938; replaced by the bicameral Congress after the 1940 amendments.
classes.disposition_reason: District returns for 1935 and 1938 survive only in printed reports of the Department of the Interior; no government body publishes them online.

classes.name: Pambansang Asamblea ng KALIBAPI (1943)
classes.name_en: National Assembly of the Second Republic (1943)
classes.note: Under Japanese occupation, provincial governors and city mayors chose 54 assemblymen on 20 September 1943 from KALIBAPI nominees; the other 54 seats were held ex officio by governors and mayors.
classes.disposition_reason: Indirect choice by appointed governors and mayors under occupation, with no popular vote.

classes.name: Batasang Pambansa
classes.note: Unicameral parliament under the 1973 Constitution: the Interim Batasang Pambansa elected 7 April 1978 by regional multi-member block vote (165 seats), and the regular Batasang Pambansa elected 14 May 1984 from provinces and cities (183 elective seats); sectoral and appointed members besides. Abolished by Proclamation No. 3 in 1986.
classes.disposition_reason: COMELEC publishes no 1978 or 1984 returns online; the official canvass survives only in print.

classes.name: Halalan ng mga delegado sa Kumbensiyong Konstitusyonal
classes.note: Delegates elected by district to the 1934 Constitutional Convention (202 delegates, 10 July 1934) and the 1971 Constitutional Convention (320 delegates, 10 November 1970). The 1986 Constitutional Commission was appointed. The 1987 Constitution lets Congress call a convention by law (Art. XVII).
classes.disposition_reason: Delegate returns for 1934 and 1970 are not published online by any government body.

dates.note: Delegates to the 1971 Constitutional Convention.

classes.name: Kongreso ng Malolos (1898)
classes.note: Delegates to the Revolutionary Congress of the First Republic were partly elected by town notables in provinces under revolutionary control in mid-1898 and partly appointed.
classes.disposition_reason: Restricted elections by town principales in some provinces, mixed with appointments, with no surviving official returns.

classes.name: Pambansang plebisito at reperendum
classes.finest_note: Provincial tallies appear only in printed proclamations; nothing after 1987 has been held.
classes.note: A constitutional amendment or revision is valid only when ratified by a majority of votes in a plebiscite (1987 Constitution, Art. XVII, Sec. 4); RA 6735 provides national initiative and referendum on laws, though the Supreme Court held it inadequate for constitutional initiatives (Santiago v. COMELEC, 1997). No national vote since 1987.

classes.note: A recall petition signed by a share of the voters leads to a recall election in which the official runs against challengers (RA 7160, Sec. 69-75, as amended by RA 9244). COMELEC lists recall elections for mayor in Puerto Princesa (8 May 2015) and Cabadbaran City (5 May 2018); earlier ones include Puerto Princesa in 2002.

classes.name: Lokal na plebisito
classes.name_en: Local plebiscites (creation, division, merger, and conversion of local units)
classes.finest_note: COMELEC posts the calendar resolution for each plebiscite; results appear only in the board of canvassers' certificates.
classes.note: No province, city, municipality, or barangay may be created, divided, merged, abolished, or substantially altered without approval in a plebiscite in the units directly affected (Art. X, Sec. 10; RA 7160, Sec. 10), e.g. the division of Maguindanao (17 September 2022), the rejected division of Palawan (13 March 2021), and city conversions. Local initiatives and referendums on ordinances under RA 6735 and RA 7160 belong here too.

classes.note: Presidents of the municipal and city chapters of the Liga ng mga Barangay and of the Pederasyon ng mga Sangguniang Kabataan are elected by and from the punong barangays and SK chairpersons and sit ex officio in the city, municipal, and provincial councils (RA 7160, Sec. 491-507; RA 10742).
classes.disposition_reason: Indirect elections among elected barangay and SK officials, run by the leagues rather than COMELEC, with no public returns.

classes.name: Halalan sa Punong Barangay
classes.finest_note: Manual count by precinct, canvassed by the barangay board of canvassers; COMELEC publishes no returns.
classes.note: One punong barangay per barangay by plurality, nonpartisan by law (RA 7160, RA 9164). The 1 December 2025 and 2 November 2026 votes were postponed by RA 12232 and RA 12326, which fixed five-year terms; the next synchronized election is in November 2028.
classes.disposition_reason: Counts are manual and canvassed in each of 42,000 barangays; COMELEC publishes no vote counts, only proclaimed winners.
